page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / No smoke without fire
title: No smoke without fire
topic: Language to use in an emergency
description:
Emergency at Tip Top Trading! Everyone has evacuated the offices following a fire alarm and Anna has to take charge. Is this a real fire emergency or just a drill? Can anything get any worse - well possibly, especially when a man from America turns up unexpectedly.
This episode focuses on important phrases to use when there is a fire emergency at work.
phrases: Please leave the building and meet outside.
Use the stairs not the lift.

listening_challenge.question:
Who does Tom carry out of the building on his shoulders?
Mr Ingle.
listening_challenge.answer:
Who does Tom carry out of the building on his shoulders?
Mr Ingle.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Here.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Here Denise.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: And Paul?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, yes I'm here and there's no need to panic. That was just a fire drill – a practice.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Phew, Tip Top Trading is safe – for now. It was just a fire drill. What a busy day this is turning out to be. Hey Anna, remember next time it could be for real so are you happy about what to say if you have to take charge?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, not really.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Just keep calm and say things like:
There's no need to panic.
Please leave the building and meet outside.
Use the stairs not the lift.
And when you're outside, you could say: Is anybody missing?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, thanks, but I hope I'll never need to use them.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well done everyone. Hopefully you all know what to do in the unlikely event of a real fire. Now, to celebrate, I'm off to buy some really nice biscuits for all of us – you know, those special double-choc ones with the little orange bits. Back to work everyone.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Honestly! I was in the middle of an important call.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, and you never got see those firemen in action, did you Denise?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Look at the time. I really need to get on with my work.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, and I've got to check up on the latest football… I mean share prices. Hold on, can anyone smell smoke?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I don't believe it! The fire alarm's gone off again. I'll call you back Marge. Oh, where's Paul when you need him? Anna, you're going to have to take charge.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me? What about Tom?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It looks like Tom has gone already.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Remember Anna, use those phrases to keep everyone calm and informed about what to do.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Err… there's no need to panic. Please leave the building and meet outside.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hold on, I just need to grab my elephant dung notepad and red pen. Come on then Anna, into the lift.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No Denise. We must use the stairs not the lift.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, with my knees!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Jump up Denise, I'll carry you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Could I have your attention please.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Louder Anna. This is urgent!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Could I have your attention please! I need your full attention. Please stay calm. I'm sure there's not a fire, just a bit of smoke. Is there anybody missing?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well, there's no smoke without fire, hey Tom! Tom? Tom? Has anyone seen Tom? That's Tom coming out of the building and he's carrying someone on his shoulder!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's Mr Ingle from the warehouse!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's OK everyone… I've put the fire out… it was in the warehouse. Mr Ingle had been smoking.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Ingle!

transcript.speaker: Mr Ingle
transcript.text: Err… yeah… sorry.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Sorry indeed! Mr Ingle's in serious trouble now. But well done Anna for dealing with that emergency and getting everyone out of the building. Here are some of the phrases she used:
There's no need to panic.
Please leave the building and meet outside.
Use the stairs not the lift.
And when you're outside, you could say:
Is anybody missing?
Seems like Tom is a bit of a hero. He has his uses! But hold on, who's this?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Say Honey, looks like I've come at a good time. Have you seen a guy called Paul round here?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: He's not here, he's gone to buy some… err… biscuits. Can I help?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Yeah sugar. I'm Mr Socrates, Paul's boss and I've come to sort this business out.

transcript.speaker: Tom & Denise
transcript.text: Mr Socrates!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh no! The head of the company's in town. This means trouble. See you next time.
